title: Pivotality and the discrete derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone in the coordinatewise order, and choose a coordinate $i$ and an input $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The indicator that changing coordinate $i$ of $x$ changes the value of $f$ equals the discrete derivative $\bigl(f(x_{i\leftarrow 1})-f(x_{i\leftarrow -1})\bigr)/2$, where $x_{i\leftarrow b}$ denotes $x$ with coordinate $i$ set to $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean-valued sign function on $\{-1,1\}^n$
